output.headline: Ratifies up to $10,000 for a contractor to help Castlemont teachers use the school's FabLab
output.summary: The district is paying an individual contractor to help Castlemont High School teachers and students use the FabLab, a hands-on workshop space. The work includes teacher training, curriculum development and in-class sessions. The contract runs November 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, which began before this vote. The contract also has a COVID amendment, but the text does not describe its terms.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $21,000 for a contractor to tie Castlemont's FabLab to classes and career courses
output.summary: The district is paying an individual contractor to connect the Castlemont High School FabLab maker space to the school day, working with teachers and the Sustainable Urban Design Academy career technical education courses. The contractor also links the school-day work to the after-school FabLab program. The contract runs November 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, which began before this vote. The contract also has a COVID amendment, but the text does not describe its terms.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $27,500 for Cypress Mandela's summer construction pre-apprenticeship for 35 students
output.summary: Cypress Mandela Training Center will run a five-week summer pre-apprenticeship program in the construction trades for up to 35 district high school students. The program runs June 8 through July 10, 2020. It is paid through the High School Linked Learning Department.

output.headline: Approves a 2019-20 nonpublic school and agency master contract with Advanced Medical Personnel Services
output.summary: This master contract lets the district use Advanced Medical Personnel Services, Inc. as a nonpublic school or agency (a private provider) to serve students, as specified in the contract. It covers July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, under the terms of an earlier Board resolution. The text states no dollar amount, so the cost is not shown here.

output.headline: Approves a 2019-20 nonpublic school and agency master contract with Charis Youth Center
output.summary: This master contract lets the district use Charis Youth Center as a nonpublic school or agency (a private provider) to serve students, as specified in the contract. It covers July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, under the terms of an earlier Board resolution. The text states no dollar amount, so the cost is not shown here.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $15,000 for a contractor to run cooking and gardening programs at Oakland International
output.summary: The district is paying an individual contractor to keep managing the cooking and gardening programs at Oakland International High School and to support new programs at Garfield Elementary and Rudsdale Newcomer School. The contract runs July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, which began before this vote. The contract also has a COVID amendment, but the text does not describe its terms.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $18,000 for UC Berkeley's college advising program at Oakland High
output.summary: The Regents of the University of California, through its Center for Educational Partnerships, will provide its Destination College Advising Corps program for students at Oakland High School. The contract runs August 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, which began before this vote. The contract also has a COVID amendment, but the text does not describe its terms.

vendor.name: The Regents of the University of California, Center for Educational Partnerships

output.headline: Approves up to $112,000 for Soccer Without Borders to serve newly arrived refugee students
output.summary: Soccer Without Borders will organize weekly soccer games with transportation for at least 100 newly arrived refugee and asylum-seeking students. It will also run a week-long summer 2020 soccer camp for up to 200 students and after-school soccer for up to 100 students during the summer of 2020. The contract period is July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, which began before this vote. The contract also has a COVID amendment, but the text does not describe its terms.

output.headline: Pays Anthonio, Inc. $18,800 to inspect construction of Sankofa Elementary's portable classrooms
output.summary: Anthonio, Inc. will serve as the Inspector of Record for the Sankofa Elementary School portable classroom project, providing daily reports, a punch list and the close-out reports required by the Division of the State Architect. The amount includes a $5,000 contingency fee. The inspector was chosen through a request-for-proposals process, and the text says competitive bidding was not required because the cost is under the bidding threshold and the work needs specially trained services. Work is scheduled from March 26, 2020 to December 31, 2021.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $50,000 for Bertrand, Fox, Elliott, Osman & Wenzel to give the district legal advice
output.summary: The district is hiring the San Francisco law firm Bertrand, Fox, Elliott, Osman & Wenzel to provide legal services as needed. The agreement is called a memorandum of understanding and engagement policy, but it is a paid legal engagement. It runs February 21 through June 30, 2020, which began before this vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $60,000 for Refugee Transitions to support newly arrived refugee families
output.summary: Refugee Transitions will teach a month-long English class for up to 90 refugee adults, provide home-based tutoring and mentoring for at least 20 refugee students, and supply two Community Navigators (one Mam-speaking, one Arabic-speaking) to help refugees who speak less common languages. It will also offer arts and crafts for children ages 4 to 6. The contract period is July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, which began before this vote. The contract also has a COVID amendment, but the text does not describe its terms.

output.headline: Approves Personnel Report No. 1920-0008
output.summary: The Board is asked to approve Personnel Report No. 1920-0008. The official text gives no details about the individual personnel actions or any dollar amounts in the report.

output.headline: Adds $8,100 to S Meek Architecture's contract for Sankofa Elementary portable classrooms
output.summary: This amendment adds $8,100 to the architectural services agreement with S Meek Architecture, raising the limit from $29,220 to $37,320. The work is for portable classrooms with restrooms needed because Sankofa Elementary School and Kaiser Elementary are merging. All other terms of the agreement stay the same.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $9,488 for the Museum of Children's Arts to teach art at Laurel Elementary
output.summary: The Museum of Children's Arts (MOCA) will provide teaching artists to teach 80 art lessons in eight classrooms at Laurel Elementary School. The contract runs February 10 through May 29, 2020, which began before this vote. The contract also has a COVID amendment, but the text does not describe its terms.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $37,500 for 14 Caliber to market the central kitchen and school meal program
output.summary: The district is paying 14 Caliber LLC, a Chicago company, for marketing and brand support for the Nutrition Services Department. The goal is to launch the central kitchen, a food education program and an instructional farm, and to get more students to eat school meals. The work period began February 3, 2020, before this vote, and runs through June 30, 2020.

output.headline: Adopts an amendment to Board Policy 5141.21 on giving medication and monitoring student health
output.summary: The Board is asked to adopt an amendment to Board Policy 5141.21, Administering Medication and Monitoring Health Conditions, which is part of the policies on students. The official text does not say what the amendment changes.

output.headline: Approves up to $10,000 for Oakland Public Education Fund to pay student interns at Dewey Academy
output.summary: Oakland Public Education Fund will manage the stipend (payment) process for student interns in the summer internship program ECCCO (Exploring College, Career, and Community Options) at Dewey Academy. The contract runs February 28 through May 28, 2020. The contract also has a COVID amendment, but the text does not describe its terms.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $13,000 for Paul Dresher Ensemble to teach music at Elmhurst United Middle
output.summary: Paul Dresher Ensemble will provide extra music instruction at Elmhurst United Middle School in strings, mariachi, percussion and jazz. The contract runs January 6 through May 29, 2020, which began before this vote. The contract also has a COVID amendment, but the text does not describe its terms.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $12,500 for Blueprint Schools Network math tutors at Elmhurst United Middle
output.summary: Blueprint Schools Network, Inc. will provide two full-time Math Fellows to give small-group, intensive math tutoring during the school day at Elmhurst United Middle School. The contract runs January 6 through May 29, 2020, which began before this vote. The contract also has a COVID amendment, but the text does not describe its terms.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $7,950 for Challenge Day to lead social-emotional activities at Urban Promise Academy
output.summary: Challenge Day will lead students and teachers at Urban Promise Academy in 6.5 hours of social and emotional activities. The activities help students notice oppression and isolation, practice safe ways to step in during conflict, and act for change in their schools and communities. The contract runs February 24 through March 13, 2020, which began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $14,800 for Idea Builder Labs to review Castlemont's FabLab operations
output.summary: Idea Builder Labs LLC will review how the Castlemont High School FabLab, a hands-on workshop space, is run and used, and will be available for support. The contract runs January 27 through June 30, 2020, which began before this vote. The contract also has a COVID amendment, but the text does not describe its terms.

output.headline: Approves up to $7,500 for Oakland Public Education Fund to supply a teaching artist for Oakland International
output.summary: Oakland Public Education Fund will supply a Youth Beat Teaching Artist for 84 hours of curriculum preparation and teaching for Oakland International High School students in an internship at KDOL. The contract runs January 6 through June 30, 2020, which began before this vote. The contract also has a COVID amendment, but the text does not describe its terms.

output.headline: Approves up to $35,000 for SPAAT to provide academic support at McClymonds High
output.summary: Student Program for Academic & Athletic Transitioning (SPAAT) will provide its College & Career Performance Initiative at McClymonds High School. It builds tutoring, academic counseling, college advising and service coordination into the African American Male Achievement Program and Oakland Athletic League programs. The contract period is August 13, 2019 through May 28, 2020, which began before this vote. The contract also has a COVID amendment, but the text does not describe its terms.

vendor.name: Student Program for Academic & Athletic Transitioning (SPAAT)

output.headline: Ratifies up to $15,000 for Public Health Institute's public health career academy at Castlemont
output.summary: Public Health Institute will continue working with students, teachers, district staff and community partners on an academy at Castlemont High School that gives Oakland students a pathway into public health careers. The contract runs February 3 through June 30, 2020, which began before this vote. The contract also has a COVID amendment, but the text does not describe its terms.

output.headline: Approves $2,275 for Youth Together to run lunchtime activities at Skyline High
output.summary: Youth Together will coordinate activities at lunchtime at Skyline High School to support students' safety and well-being and their social, emotional and physical development. The contract period is August 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, which began before this vote. The contract also has a COVID amendment, but the text does not describe its terms.

output.headline: Repeals an inadvertently approved $20,000 East Bay Asian Youth Center contract for Edna Brewer
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The item repeals Enactment No. 20-0600 dated May 13, 2020, which is after this March 25, 2020 meeting, so the date may be misprinted.
output.summary: The Board is repealing an earlier approval of a professional services contract and COVID amendment with East Bay Asian Youth Center (EBAYC) for Edna Brewer Middle School, worth $20,000. The text says the earlier approval was made inadvertently.

output.headline: Awards Bay Alarm up to $90,000 to monitor break-in, vandalism and fire alarms at district sites
output.summary: Bay Alarm Company will monitor break-in, vandalism and fire alarms at the district sites listed in the agreement. The cost is $6,000 per month, up to $90,000 in total, from April 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021. It is paid through the Buildings and Grounds Department.

output.headline: Awards Bay Alarm up to $45,000 for burglary alarm response and patrol at district sites
output.summary: Bay Alarm Company will respond to burglary alarms and provide outside patrols, 24 hours a day, seven days a week, at the district sites listed in the agreement. The cost is $15,000 per month, up to $45,000 in total, for April 1 through June 30, 2020. It is paid through the Police Services Department.

output.headline: Approves up to $11.5M a year for Zum to provide special education buses with seat belts

money.evidence: not to exceed $11,500,000.00 per contract year

output.summary: Zum Services, Inc. will provide special education transportation vehicles with seat belts for district school sites and programs. The first term runs August 1, 2020 through July 31, 2025, with a limit of $11,500,000 per contract year. The district may extend it for up to five more one-year terms, and if it does, the yearly amount can rise by no more than 2 percent each year.

output.headline: Approves the district's 2020-2021 school year calendar
output.summary: The Board is asked to approve the K-12 academic calendar for the 2020-2021 school year. The official text does not list the specific dates.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $30,000 for Sports Management Resources to review girls' athletics

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $30,000.00

output.summary: The Board is ratifying (approving) a contract with Sports Management Resources of Shelton, Connecticut, for an analysis and recommendations on the benefits and treatment of female student athletes. The work may include reviewing participation data, assessing athletic facilities, running workshops for district staff and surveying girls' interest in sports. It runs from March 25, 2020 through March 25, 2021 and may not cost more than $30,000.
